v.why: Restoring the direct input-to-output residual path where none existed gives much larger gains than swapping skip in for an existing op (exps 7, 11, 12 vs 8-10, 13).
Deleting the skip residual is far more damaging than deleting a conv on edge 3, because the skip is what makes deep stacked cells trainable (exps 38, 39 vs 41-43).
With edge 1 already absent, removing edge 0 disconnects nodes 1 and 2 entirely, leaving only edge 3, so the cell collapses (exps 18, 19).
When edge 0 is none, node 1 receives no input, so a conv on edge 4 has nothing to process and adds no capacity (exp 64 vs 61, 63).
In conv-heavy cells, replacing the skip residual with another conv removes the shortcut and hurts, while in skip/pool cells it adds needed capacity (exps 72, 76 vs 73, 74).
If edge 4 is absent, edge 5 may be the last learned path into the output, so removing it is catastrophic (exp 99 vs 98).
Swapping a parametric conv for parameter-free pooling on the main output edge costs more than swapping out skip or none.
With node 1 disconnected, edge 2 carries no signal, so adding a conv there brings no benefit.
Without the edge-3 residual, removing another output-feeding edge cuts the remaining paths to node 3 and hurts much more.
Adding a conv where edge 5 was empty creates a new path from node 2 to the output, which helps more than replacing an existing op.

raw:
I based these hypotheses on the 99 experiments and on how the cell's graph is wired. Most of them rest on three effects:

- **The residual path.** Edge 3 (node 0 → node 3) is the cell's direct shortcut from input to output. Whether it is `none`, `skip_connect` or a convolution changes how much almost any other edit matters.
- **Disconnected nodes.** If edge 0 is `none`, node 1 gets no input. Edges 2 and 4 then carry nothing, so edits on them have little effect.
- **Removing the last route to the output.** Deleting an edge (`none`) is very costly when it is the last remaining path from input to output, and cheap when other paths exist.

Hypotheses with the strongest support in the data:

- **Edge 3 → skip_connect is better when edge 3 is currently none.** Experiments 7, 11 and 12 gain more than 13 and the others.
- **Edge 3 → none is worse when edge 3 is currently skip_connect.** Experiments 38 and 39 lose more than 41 to 43.
- **Edge 5 → none is worse when edge 4 is none.** Compare experiment 99 with 98.

Among the rest, three have only one or two supporting data points (edge 0 → none when edge 1 is none, experiments 18 and 19; edge 4 → nor_conv_3x3 when edge 0 is none, experiment 64; edge 3 → nor_conv_3x3 when edge 4 is nor_conv_3x3, experiments 72 and 76). Edge 2 → nor_conv_3x3 when edge 0 is none, and edge 4 → none when edge 3 is none, are untested and rest only on the wiring argument. Edge 5 → nor_conv_3x3 when edge 5 is none is a prior about adding a path versus replacing one.
